principles: Claim admissibility is always mechanically enforced and hash-bound
No overclaim: do not equate control machinery with scientific correctness
Prefer minimal, bounded extension over broad domain rewrite
Keep benchmark scope stable except control-regime axis
Retain non-authority/no-production default unless explicit stronger-readiness stories exist
drivers: Keep boundary semantics aligned with Proof-or-Stop
Enable reproducible validation of claim control

options.name: Docs-first only
cons: No executable gate or benchmark proof

options.name: MVP schema+gate extension
pros: Provides deterministic rejection of stale/mismatched evidence

rationale: This option gives concrete claim-admissibility mechanics first while keeping scope bounded, and it allows incremental hardening via benchmark and reporting tasks in later milestones.

preMortem.scenario: mismatch between identity fields and lifecycle transition checks
preMortem.trigger: Schema binding not applied consistently in gate check
preMortem.mitigation: Fail-closed checks on spec/training/config/grid/checkpoint hash continuity

preMortem.scenario: benchmark compares task variants, not control regimes
preMortem.consequence: reported gain is invalid and overclaims become likely
preMortem.mitigation: Pin all task settings and random seeds in a shared benchmark harness contract

preMortem.scenario: overclaim wording leaks into public docs
preMortem.consequence: project credibility and review boundaries degrade
preMortem.mitigation: Use explicit claim-boundary paragraph and keep PDE correctness exclusions
